name: Parallel park reliably
blurb: A reference-point procedure, not a knack. Learn the three markers for your car and it becomes repeatable rather than a gamble.
gear: Two cones, or a quiet street with real gaps
steps: Find a gap about one and a half car lengths, signal, and pull alongside the front car with your rear wheels roughly level with its rear bumper.
Reverse straight until your rear wheels line up with the other car’s rear bumper — your first fixed reference point.
Turn the wheel fully towards the kerb and reverse until your car sits at roughly 45 degrees.
Straighten the wheel and reverse until your front bumper clears the other car’s rear corner.
Turn fully the other way and reverse in, then straighten up and adjust.
Practise with cones until it takes one attempt, then practise on real streets.
tips: Go slowly and steer fast. Almost every failed park is from moving too quickly.
Reference points differ per car. Recalibrate when you drive something unfamiliar.
proof: You park in a gap only slightly longer than the car, first attempt, without touching the kerb.
